Alexandre Berthier, 3rd Prince of Wagram, was a French nobleman and prince of Wagram. Born on March 24, 1836, in Paris, he was the son of Napoléon Alexandre Berthier and Zénaïde Françoise Clary. He was the grandson of General Jean-Baptiste Berthier, who had been Chief of Staff to Napoleon I. Berthier married Bertha Clara von Rothschild in 1882 and they had three children, all of whom are buried at the Château de Grosbois. His collection of modern paintings, acquired through instinctive purchases and shrewd selection, was valued at forty to fifty million francs today. Berthier's collection included works by artists such as Courbet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Cézanne, Monet, Sisley, Pissarro, Puvis de Chavannes, Degas, and Manet. His reputation as a collector of modern art was noted, but recent historical studies have led to a relativization of this image. Berthier's collection was documented in the Berthier family archives, which were bequeathed to the Archives Nationales. Wikipedia
